newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai opens whole city for residence permits.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai opens whole city for residence permits.

text.p: People from outside Shanghai may now obtain residence permits for anywhere in the city if they buy apartments worth at least 400,000 yuan and with a floor area of 80 square metres or more, a city official said on Thursday.

The government last month started to give out-of-city residents permits to buy apartments in the Pudong New Area, and now has extended the plan to all areas of Shanghai to stimulate the city's sluggish housing market, the official said.
Pudong has already sold 41 such apartments to people from outside the city, and 4,000 other people have registered for information about the plan, the People's Daily said on Thursday.
Purchasers must pay the whole amount before receiving the residence permit and cannot resell the apartment for five years.
Most Shanghai people prefer to live in Puxi on the western side of the Huangpu river, rather than in Pudong on the east.
Puxi is the city's commercial, residential and industrial area, and transport links are poor to Pudong, which the city wants to turn into the Manhattan of Asia.
Shanghai has at least four million square metres of unoccupied commercial apartments, the Business News reported last month.
